patch.head: working-tree afterimage described by afterimage.json SHA256 ece77d1f5ff1040ac72fdbd3a8865ad4c138f27a1bf6706ca00a62ebcac6ee9c

impact.rationale: The patch changes durable authorization, scheduler, command, candidate, and audit state. Its main-store v1 wire change deterministically prevents rollback to the old strict decoder after the first automated command.

regressionLikelihood.rationale: The legacy incompatibility is reached by the advertised happy path because Automated=true serializes a new field into subscription-store/v1. Capacity and source-contract weaknesses are also source-visible rather than speculative.

regressionProtection.rationale: The afterimage, strict patch reversal, 12 declared new Go tops, generation/restart/clock tests, and relevant-package CI lane are useful. They do not test old-binary reopening of an automated main store, semantic sidecar truth tables, two-store crash cuts, durable reservation, or the exact combined 700-top/source closure.

recoverability.rationale: Once an automated command has written the new field, an old binary cannot reopen the v1 main store without an explicit migration or byte rewrite. Independent sidecar/main-store rollback can also lose or replay cross-store truth because no common checkpoint or anti-rollback root exists.

confidence.rationale: The primary compatibility defect follows directly from the new JSON field, unchanged v1 schema, and old DisallowUnknownFields decoder. Other findings are tied to exact source branches; Go/runtime evidence remains explicitly unrun.

applicability.rationale: The patch is the named immutable P207A v2 delivery, its size and SHA-256 match, all 27 afterimage hashes match, reverse apply and diff-check pass, and the source-only verifier reports PASS.

statusQuoRisk.rationale: Without this patch automatic refresh remains unavailable, but current manual subscription and Accepted LKV behavior remain established. That does not justify accepting a rollback-breaking durable wire change.

materialBoundaries.invariant: A P207A automated attempt must not make subscription-store/v1 unreadable by the old strict decoder when the feature is disabled or rolled back.
materialBoundaries.runtimeRoot: subscription ControlCommand persistence and OpenStore decoder
materialBoundaries.counterexample: ControlCommand adds automated,omitempty and ExecuteRefresh persists Automated=true while storeSchema remains chengwang.subscription-store/v1; the old ControlCommand lacks the field and storeDecode uses DisallowUnknownFields.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Keep v1 bytes unchanged, or introduce an explicit main-store schema migration plus backup/rollback tooling and old/new compatibility tests. A sidecar alone is insufficient.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Normal binding change, delete/re-add, restart, and sequence exhaustion must not reuse an attempt key or fence.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: No forward-path reuse was found: ledger generation is retained across deletion, LastSequence is global and persisted, the key binds generation/sequence/seal, and MaxUint64 blocks.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Retain the current ledger and sequence checks and run the declared Linux tests on the integrated exact head.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Restoring stale scheduler bytes, alone or with a stale main-store backup, must not revive a consumed attempt identity or silently advertise a candidate absent from the main store.
materialBoundaries.runtimeRoot: independent subscription-refresh-v2 and subscriptions store directories
materialBoundaries.counterexample: The sidecar has no checkpoint tied to the current main-store root and no external monotonic anchor. Restoring an older canonical sidecar restores IdentityKey, generation and LastSequence; restoring both stores can replay a previously consumed network attempt, while restoring only main can leave a terminal sidecar pointing at a missing candidate.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Add a common durable checkpoint/epoch or explicit coordinated backup/restore refusal and crash-cut/rollback tests before durability acceptance.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Only a source-owned post-open recovery capability may resume a persisted running attempt; a live caller flag must not choose restart authority.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: Claim is exported and accepts recovering bool. The in-memory recovery map limits use to one persisted running record, but the first caller supplying true selects and consumes the restart entitlement.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Return or retain an opaque one-use recovery capability from OpenRefreshStore and keep ordinary live Claim unable to request recovery.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Every accepted canonical sidecar must represent a producer-reachable state with exact per-state fields and ledger high-water consistency.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: Validation checks broad field syntax but permits impossible combinations such as succeeded_noop with no NextAttemptAt, candidate_quarantined without candidate/audit evidence, idle carrying completion metadata, or a ledger LastIssuedSequence unrelated to the active attempt.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Add an exact state/field truth table, bind active AttemptSequence to its ledger high-water, and include malformed canonical JSON negative tests.

materialBoundaries.invariant: A claimed automatic attempt must own enough command, candidate and audit capacity before Fetch so concurrent manual work cannot consume it.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: Store.Capacity releases the main-store mutex before ExecuteRefresh. A concurrent manual command can consume the checked slot before RecordControlPrepared or Import; there is no durable reservation spanning sidecar and main store.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Implement the acknowledged durable reservation/active-command slice. Until then describe the check as advisory preflight and do not treat it as a capacity guarantee.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Automatic refresh may add only a quarantined candidate and must not delete manual command records, audit history, UNKNOWN, approvals, or the current Accepted LKV.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: No deletion or admission path was added. The candidate test checks AcceptedCandidateID remains unchanged, and fixed capacity fails closed rather than compacting records.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Preserve these semantics in the later retention/checkpoint slice and prove them under near-limit and crash-cut Linux tests.

materialBoundaries.invariant: The dedicated lane must bind every runtime dependency and reconstruct the exact prior 688 plus 12 new top-level tests.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: The verifier hashes only 27 changed files, asserts baselineGoTopCount==688 as metadata, and checks the 12 names are a subset of tops found in seven test files. It does not enumerate the prior 688, prove total 700, or bind unchanged persistence dependencies such as store_linux.go.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Derive a full dependency manifest and exact combined top set from the integrated head, then run the same exact package list and formatting/source checks.

validation.protects: Patch is 116136 bytes with the supplied SHA-256; DELIVERY.md and afterimage.json hashes match; all 27 candidate file byte counts/SHA-256 values match and are LF-only.

validation.protects: git apply --check --reverse --binary succeeds on the candidate and git diff --check exits zero.

validation.protects: check_source_contract.py reports PASS for its declared 27-source/12-new-top model; this does not establish its missing full closure.

validation.name: Independent new-top comparison
validation.protects: Across the seven declared test files, baseline 81 tops become 93 with exactly the declared 12 additions and no removals.

validation.name: Old strict-decoder rollback proof
validation.protects: Static comparison proves old ControlCommand has no automated field while old storeDecode disallows unknown fields under the same v1 schema.

validation.name: Go compile, gofmt, unit/race, Linux filesystem and runtime
validation.protects: Forbidden by task constraints and explicitly not claimed.

validation.name: Two-store crash cuts, stale backup restore, near-limit concurrency and long-run fairness
validation.protects: Not implemented or executed; these are required before controlled Linux validation.

unknowns.summary: The candidate has not compiled or run on Linux; the exact 12 new Go tops, secure filesystem paths, timers, race behavior and close ordering remain unproven.

Long-duration RefreshCommands/checkpoint/archive, durable reservation, migration backup/rollback, and retention thresholds are explicitly absent; >4096/no-op and near-16MiB automation cannot be accepted as indefinitely operable.
Real 1/2/32-source fairness, blocking Fetch identity replacement, TLS/API restart, filesystem fault injection and two-store crash-cut outcomes are untested.
